thm:projection-composed-directional-limi.proof_tex:
Put \(d=|\mathcal O|\) and \(\Phi=\theta\circ\Pi_{\mathfrak O}\).  We first differentiate the Euclidean projection without an interior-point assumption.  Let \(t_k\downarrow0\), let \(g_k\to g\) in \(\mathbb R^d\), and set
\[
x_k=p+t_kg_k,
\qquad
q_k=\Pi_{\mathfrak O}(x_k),
\qquad
d_k=\frac{q_k-p}{t_k}.
\tag{1}
\]
Because \(p\in\mathfrak O\), the minimizing property of \(q_k\) gives
\[
\|q_k-x_k\|_2\leq\|p-x_k\|_2=t_k\|g_k\|_2,
\]
and hence \(\|d_k\|_2\leq2\|g_k\|_2\).  Thus \((d_k)\) is bounded.  Projection onto the nonempty closed convex polytope \(\mathfrak O\) is characterized by the first-order inequality
\[
\langle x_k-q_k,v-q_k\rangle\leq0
\qquad(v\in\mathfrak O).
\tag{2}
\]
Every subsequential limit \(d_*\) of \((d_k)\) belongs to \(T_{\mathfrak O}(p)\) by the definition of that closed tangent cone.  If \(z\) is radial, meaning \(p+\varepsilon z\in\mathfrak O\) for some \(\varepsilon>0\), convexity implies \(p+t_kz\in\mathfrak O\) for all sufficiently large \(k\).  Substitute this point for \(v\) in (2), divide by \(t_k^2\), and pass along a subsequence for which \(d_k\to d_*\).  This gives
\[
\langle g-d_*,z-d_*\rangle\leq0.
\tag{3}
\]
Radial directions are dense in \(T_{\mathfrak O}(p)\) by its defining closure, so (3) holds for every \(z\) in that cone.  Expanding squared distances shows that (3) is equivalent to
\[
\|g-d_*\|_2\leq\|g-z\|_2
\qquad(z\in T_{\mathfrak O}(p)).
\]
Strict convexity gives the unique minimizer, so
\[
d_*=\Pi_{T_{\mathfrak O}(p)}g.
\tag{4}
\]
Every convergent subsequence has the same limit and the original sequence is bounded; hence the whole sequence converges to (4).  This proves Hadamard directional differentiability of \(\Pi_{\mathfrak O}\) at \(p\), with derivative \(g\mapsto\Pi_{T_{\mathfrak O}(p)}g\).

We next derive the endpoint derivatives from finiteness.  The observable--target set
\[
\mathcal C=\operatorname{conv}\{(B_{\cdot,t},h_e(t)):t\in\mathcal T_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\}
\tag{5}
\]
is a finite polytope.  Eliminating the finitely many simplex coordinates from its defining finite system of linear equalities and inequalities gives a finite half-space representation of \(\mathcal C\).  Solving those inequalities for the last coordinate shows that there are finite index sets \(R_L,R_U\) and dual-feasible affine functions
\[
\ell_r(x)=\alpha_r+\lambda_r^{\top}x\quad(r\in R_L),
\qquad
u_s(x)=\bar\alpha_s+\bar\lambda_s^{\top}x\quad(s\in R_U)
\]
such that, throughout \(\mathfrak O\),
\[
L(x)=\max_{r\in R_L}\ell_r(x),
\qquad
U(x)=\min_{s\in R_U}u_s(x).
\tag{6}
\]
For completeness, dual feasibility follows by evaluating each supporting inequality on every generator in (5): it gives \(\alpha_r\mathbf 1+B^{\top}\lambda_r\leq h_e\) for lower supports and \(\bar\alpha_s\mathbf 1+B^{\top}\bar\lambda_s\geq h_e\) for upper supports.  Conversely, multiplying either columnwise inequality by feasible simplex weights proves weak duality, so the active supports in (6) attain the corresponding dual value.

Let
\[
R_L(p)=\{r:\ell_r(p)=L(p)\},
\qquad
R_U(p)=\{s:u_s(p)=U(p)\}.
\]
Because the families are finite, every inactive affine function has a strictly positive gap at \(p\).  Hence, if \(z_k\to z\) and \(p+t_kz_k\in\mathfrak O\), inactive indices cannot optimize for all sufficiently large \(k\), and
\[
\frac{L(p+t_kz_k)-L(p)}{t_k}
\longrightarrow\max_{r\in R_L(p)}\lambda_r^{\top}z,
\tag{7}
\]
\[
\frac{U(p+t_kz_k)-U(p)}{t_k}
\longrightarrow\min_{s\in R_U(p)}\bar\lambda_s^{\top}z.
\tag{8}
\]
These finite active-index formulas agree with optimization over the entire unnormalized optimal faces.  Indeed, if \((\alpha,\lambda)\in\Lambda_L(p)\), dual feasibility gives
\[
\alpha+\lambda^{\top}(p+t_kz_k)\leq L(p+t_kz_k),
\qquad
\alpha+\lambda^{\top}p=L(p).
\]
Subtract, divide by \(t_k\), and use (7) to obtain
\[
\lambda^{\top}z\leq\max_{r\in R_L(p)}\lambda_r^{\top}z.
\]
Every active pair in (7) belongs to \(\Lambda_L(p)\), so equality holds after maximizing over the full face.  The analogous upper-dual argument gives
\[
L'_p(z)=\max_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\Lambda_L(p)}\lambda^{\top}z,
\qquad
U'_p(z)=\min_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\Lambda_U(p)}\lambda^{\top}z.
\tag{9}
\]
These expressions are gauge invariant on the tangent cone: every \(z\in T_{\mathfrak O}(p)\) satisfies \(\mathbf 1^{\top}z=0\), and replacing \((\alpha,\lambda)\) by \((\alpha-c,\lambda+c\mathbf 1)\) leaves \(\lambda^{\top}z\) unchanged.

For the sequence in (1), equation (4) gives \(d_k\to z=\Pi_{T_{\mathfrak O}(p)}g\).  Apply (7)--(9) to \(q_k=p+t_kd_k\).  We obtain
\[
\frac{\Phi(p+t_kg_k)-\Phi(p)}{t_k}
\longrightarrow
\left(
\max_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\Lambda_L(p)}\lambda^{\top}z,
\min_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\Lambda_U(p)}\lambda^{\top}z
\right)
=\Gamma'_p(g).
\tag{10}
\]
Thus \(\Phi\) is Hadamard directionally differentiable at \(p\).  The derivative is continuous because projection onto a closed convex cone is nonexpansive and the two endpoint coordinates in (9) are finite piecewise-linear functions on the tangent cone.  Multiple active projection faces and multiple optimal LP bases remain inside the projection, maximum, and minimum in (10).

It remains to derive the stochastic limit.  Under \(\text{ass:iid-finite-sampling}\), write \(X_i=\mathbf e_{O_i}-p\).  These vectors are independent, centered, bounded, and have covariance \(\Sigma_p\).  For every \(a\in\mathbb R^d\) and \(u\in\mathbb R\), Taylor expansion with a remainder bounded uniformly by a constant times \(n^{-3/2}|a^{\top}X_i|^3\) gives
\[
\mathbb E\exp\!\left(\frac{iu a^{\top}X_i}{\sqrt n}\right)
=1-\frac{u^2a^{\top}\Sigma_pa}{2n}+O(n^{-3/2}).
\]
Raising this characteristic function to the \(n\)-th power yields
\[
\mathbb E\exp\!\left(iu a^{\top}\sqrt n(\widehat p-p)\right)
\longrightarrow\exp\!\left(-\frac{u^2a^{\top}\Sigma_pa}{2}\right).
\tag{11}
\]
Thus every linear contrast converges to the corresponding contrast of \(G_p\), including zero-variance contrasts, and the joint characteristic functions converge to that of \(G_p\).  Hence
\[
X_n:=\sqrt n(\widehat p-p)\rightsquigarrow G_p.
\tag{12}
\]

Define \(f_n(g)=\sqrt n\{\Phi(p+g/\sqrt n)-\Phi(p)\}\).  Equation (10) says that whenever \(g_n\to g\), one has \(f_n(g_n)\to\Gamma'_p(g)\).  This sequential property is uniform on every compact set: otherwise a violating sequence in a compact set would have a convergent subsequence contradicting (10) and continuity of \(\Gamma'_p\).  Since (12) makes \((X_n)\) tight, for every bounded continuous test function \(\psi\), uniform convergence on a compact set carrying arbitrarily high probability gives
\[
\mathbb E\psi(f_n(X_n))-\mathbb E\psi(\Gamma'_p(X_n))\longrightarrow0.
\]
Continuity of \(\Gamma'_p\) and (12) give \(\Gamma'_p(X_n)\rightsquigarrow\Gamma'_p(G_p)\).  Since \(p\in\mathfrak O\), \(\Phi(p)=\theta(p)\), and \(\text{def:projection-endpoint-estimator}\) gives \(\Phi(\widehat p)=\widehat\theta\).  Therefore
\[
\sqrt n\{\widehat\theta-\theta(p)\}
\rightsquigarrow\Gamma'_p(G_p),
\]
with no projection-face or optimal-basis uniqueness assumption.

snapshot.stmt: For every fixed \(p\in\mathfrak O\), the map \(x\mapsto\theta(\Pi_{\mathfrak O}x)\) is Hadamard directionally differentiable at \(p\) with derivative \(\Gamma'_p\), and \(\sqrt n\{\widehat\theta-\theta(p)\}\rightsquigarrow\Gamma'_p(G_p)\). This formula remains valid when \(p\) is on a projection face and either endpoint has multiple optimal bases.

defs.def:projection-composed-derivative:
For a direction \(g\), put \(z=\Pi_{T_{\mathfrak O}(p)}g\).  Using the full unnormalized dual faces, define
\[
\Gamma'_p(g)=\left(
\max_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\Lambda_L(p)}\lambda^{\top}z,
\min_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\Lambda_U(p)}\lambda^{\top}z
\right).
\]
Only the slope coordinate acts on \(z\); no normalized representative is selected.
defs.def:projection-endpoint-estimator: Project \(\widehat p\) onto \(\mathfrak O\) in Euclidean norm and evaluate both endpoint programs: \(\widehat\theta=\theta(\Pi_{\mathfrak O}\widehat p)\).

prop:trialed-policy-reduction.proof_tex:
Suppose first that \(c_e(s)=c_{j^\star}(s)\) for every \(s\in\mathcal S\), where \(j^\star\in J_0\).  Then for every legal response type,
\[
h_e(t)=y_{c_e(s_t)}(t)=y_{c_{j^\star}(s_t)}(t).
\tag{1}
\]
The known arm law has \(\rho_{j^\star}>0\) because \(\rho\) lies in the relative interior of the trial-arm simplex.  For every compatible latent mixture \(v\), randomized assignment and the common-outcome response imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_v[Y\mid D=j^\star]
&=\rho_{j^\star}^{-1}
\sum_t v_t\rho_{j^\star}y_{c_{j^\star}(s_t)}(t)\\
&=h_e^{\top}v,
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
where (1) was used in the last equality.  The conditional mean on the left of (2) is determined by the observed law \(p\).  Consequently every \(v\) in the fiber \(\{v:Bv=p\}\) has the same target, and \(\text{prop:sharp-selective-label-interval}\) gives
\[
L(p)=U(p)=\mathbb E[Y\mid D=j^\star].
\]

For the separate revelation claim, if \(A_c=1\) for every \(c\in\mathcal C\), then the reveal-action assumption gives \(R=1\), and masked truth gives \(Z_{\mathrm{obs}}=Z\) almost surely.  Full revelation does not by itself identify a distinct untrialed configuration.  Consider one stratum, one trialed configuration \((1,q_\ell)\), one untrialed configuration \((1,q_h)\), and \(q_\ell<q_h\).  In two deterministic SCMs set \(Z=1\), set every action response to one, and set every neutral outcome to zero.  For the \(r=1\) outcome path, set
\[
(Y_{(1,q_\ell)},Y_{(1,q_h)})=(0,0)
\quad\text{in the first model},
\qquad
(Y_{(1,q_\ell)},Y_{(1,q_h)})=(0,1)
\quad\text{in the second}.
\tag{3}
\]
Both paths are nondecreasing, as correct-performance order requires for \(Z=1\).  The incorrect neutral path is constant, so neutral invariance and incorrect-performance order hold, and the correct outcomes dominate the neutral outcomes, so counterfactual correctness holds.  Both models can use the same randomized arm law and therefore belong to \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\).  Their trialed laws, including the always-revealed label \(Z=1\), coincide because both have trialed outcome zero; their untrialed means are respectively zero and one by (3).  This proves nonidentification from full revelation alone, while the first part proves identification under configuration overlap.  Special observed fibers, neutral-invariance coincidences, or additional restrictions may still collapse the sharp interval, exactly as the statement allows.

snapshot.stmt: If there is \(j^{\star}\in J_0\) with \(c_e(s)=c_{j^{\star}}(s)\) for every \(s\in\mathcal S\), then \(L(p)=U(p)=\mathbb E[Y\mid D=j^{\star}]\). Separately, if \(A_c=1\) for every \(c\in\mathcal C\), then \(Z\) is fully observed, but full revelation alone does not point-identify every distinct untrialed configuration: there exist two legal SCMs with the same fully labeled trial law and different untrialed means. Identification may nevertheless occur at special observed laws, through configuration overlap, through the neutral-invariance restriction, or under further identifying restrictions.

assumptions.ass:common-action-response: Under policy \(j\in J\) and stratum \(S=s\), the structural action is \(A=A_{c_j(s)}\).
assumptions.ass:common-outcome-response: Under policy \(j\in J\) and stratum \(S=s\), the structural outcome is \(Y=Y_{c_j(s)}\).
assumptions.ass:correct-performance-order: For every unit, \(r=Z\) and \(q\le q'\) imply \(Y_{(r,q)}\le Y_{(r,q')}\).
assumptions.ass:counterfactual-correctness: For every unit and configurations \(c=(r,q)\), \(c'=(r',q')\) in \(\mathcal C\), \(r=Z\) and \(r'\neq Z\) imply \(Y_c\ge Y_{c'}\).

prose_overlay.tldr: Repeated trials cannot accompany every updated human--AI policy, and in pretrial applications ground truth is revealed only by an endogenous action. The paper identifies the exact observable--target image of legal finite response types and makes the SLCC-specific primitive bracket-stratum construction its structural headline: an arbitrary-finite extension of the exact thirty-two-row quotient, a bracket-supported law with two exact \(199/800\) full-versus-label-blind gaps, and a small full-support mixture yielding a nonempty relative-interior region of two-sided improvement. The optimal-dual-face equivalence is used as a generic LP diagnostic for that construction. Generic simultaneous multinomial confidence-region propagation supplies a finite-sample implementation corollary. At boundary laws, Euclidean projection has the paired LP directional limit, and an explicit centered \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) subsampling schedule gives pointwise fixed-law conservative simultaneous endpoint coverage even at the certified nondegenerate zero atom; no uniform-validity, first-atom-aware, or dominance claim is made.
prose_overlay.related_work: Zhang, Skalnes, Chen, and Oberst (2026, Assumptions 3.1--3.3, Theorem 4.1, the Tightness of Bounds discussion, Theorem 5.1, and Appendix G) supply the correctness, performance-order, and neutral restrictions, but do not claim their main bounds are tight and do not treat the present endogenous reveal action. Chen and Oberst (2025, Theorems 3.1--3.2) prove attained bounds in the preceding performance-mediated model without the selective-label correctness quotient. Lakkaraju et al. (2017, p. 4 and Proposition 4.1) formalize decision-induced labels through contraction across decision makers rather than a sharp compatible-SCM fiber. Imai et al. (2023) supply the randomized PSA consumer, while Ben-Michael et al. (2025, Theorem 3 and Theorem S3) analyze classification-risk contrasts under a different baseline-potential-outcome design. Duarte et al. (2024, Proposition 1 and Theorem 1) provide generic finite response-function optimization, and Section 6 with Appendix E provides generic propagation of simultaneous observable-law confidence regions. Accordingly, the optimal-dual-face equivalence here is a generic LP restriction diagnostic, not the field-level novelty. The structural contribution is the SLCC-specific primitive bracket-stratum construction: a legal arbitrary-finite extension of the exact thirty-two-row quotient, exact bracket-supported \(199/800\) gaps, a small full-support mixture, and a nonempty relative-interior region of two-sided full-versus-label-blind improvement robust to duplicate arms, positive randomization probabilities, extra policies, performance values, and strata. Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019) provide the calibrated-projection benchmark. Fang and Santos (2019, Theorem 2.1 and Section 4) provide the directional delta method and convex-projection derivative, while the paired LP optimal-face composition is specialized here; Hong and Li (2018) provide a numerical-derivative alternative. Andrews and Guggenberger (2009, introduction at pp. 3--5) establish uniform validity for appropriate inverted moment-inequality test statistics, warn that direct subsampling of estimated-set endpoints is not uniformly valid, and record first-order equivalence of subsampling and the \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) bootstrap when the squared subsample size divided by sample size vanishes. Romano and Shaikh (2010, Theorems 2.2--2.3) obtain pointwise identified-set subsampling coverage under divergence of the subsample size, a vanishing subsample fraction, and continuity at the smallest target quantile, and uniform coverage under their high-level stochastic-ordering condition (21). Arvanitis, Scaillet, and Topaloglou (2020, Lemma 2 and Theorem 2) already allow a stochastic-spanning saddle limit to have a bounded jump at zero and obtain exactness under a significance-level versus jump-bound restriction. The distinct inference result here is narrower: fixed-law conservative simultaneous coverage for the coupled projection--LP endpoint statistic, using explicit schedules and a vanishing-slack/global-sign argument at a certified nondegenerate zero atom. It is not uniform validity, not the first atom-aware subsampling result, and does not dominate those procedures.
prose_overlay.technical_internal_limitation: The atomic-tie theorem is pointwise at a fixed observable law. It requires a finite refined fan, every retained normal and endpoint slope to be nonzero on the sampling support space, and Gaussian nondegeneracy on that space. Its Berry--Esseen constant and Boolean-event family are fixed-law objects and need not remain controlled near covariance-rank changes. The result proves conservative simultaneous coverage for the stated coupled projection--LP endpoint statistic and schedules; it does not establish uniform validity, a general endpoint-subsampling principle, exact coverage at every nominal level, or dominance over inverted-test and atom-aware spanning procedures.
prose_overlay.honest_scope: The identification results concern finite strata and policies and binary actions, labels, and outcomes. The explicit strictness certificate uses three distinct externally certified performance levels; the arbitrary-finite bracket construction permits duplicate endpoint arms, any strictly positive trial randomization probabilities, extra policies, performance values, and strata while preserving a nonempty relative-interior two-sided gain after a sufficiently small full-support perturbation. The optimal-dual-face equivalence is a generic LP restriction diagnostic supporting that construction, not a standalone field-level novelty. Generic confidence-region propagation is an implementation corollary. The projection-composed limit and atomic-tie subsampling theorem are pointwise; the latter retains all finite-fan, nonzero-restriction, Gaussian-nondegeneracy, and nonuniform-near-rank-change limitations and claims neither priority over atom-aware subsampling nor superiority to existing inverted-test procedures. Equality of the untrialed and a trialed configuration recovers the randomized observed mean. Full revelation of \(Z\) removes masking but does not identify a distinct untrialed configuration. Multiclass actions, dynamic policies, violation budgets, joint deployment targets, policy learning, and uniform boundary inference remain outside this kernel.
